issue.title: E4: Verified completion with fingerprint-bound verdict receipts
issue.description: A named verification run can mint a short-lived receipt for its exact fingerprint and trustworthy E3 verdict; users and host-owned prepared completion can query that proof, while every tool invocation still executes and any drift or uncertain failure recovers.

issue.title: Recheck E3 precision and verification inputs
issue.description: hermetic-baseline: re-run the KNOWN precision gate, inventory changing lint and bead inputs, and make check fingerprints complete within bounded probe cost.

issue.title: Add the Rust receipt contract and durable store
issue.description: rust-receipts: add additive schema-1 receipt storage, strict mint and invalidation rules, typed lookup refusals, retention, bindings, and compatibility tests.

issue.title: Pin the released core before catalog adoption
issue.description: core-pin-catalog: ratchet sase to a published receipt-capable core, create the beta flag, then declare per-tool accept and TTL policy without moving definition identity.

issue.title: Mint and query receipts on both execution paths
issue.description: receipt-execution-cli: wire foreground and handed-off settlement to Rust minting and expose a truthful receipt query with versioned JSON and exact exit codes.

issue.title: Measure content-equivalent verification repeats
issue.description: opportunity-report: list receipts and report content-addressed repeat opportunities, including dirty-tree-to-commit equivalence, without changing run behavior.

issue.title: Gate prepared completion on a covering receipt
issue.description: verdict-completion: add explicit no-new intent policy, recheck the verified tree at commit time, recover with typed refusals, and record provenance in host actions.

issue.title: Prove acceptance and remove the beta flag
issue.description: landing-proof: exercise all nine landing gates, demonstrate athena completion, document the contract, publish authorized memory and skill sources, and remove the flag.
